translations.text: Hymns of Mar Balai, chorepiscopus, on the dedication of the church newly built in the city of Qinnasrin.
Let whoever labored on your house rejoice, for he prepared a dwelling for the Lord who created him. Let him count himself blessed, whoever brought the Spirit down upon the work of his hands.
For now that it is the house of the Godhead, every kind of help is found in it. It is a dwelling on earth in which grace is held, to pour out mercy.
He sits in his house and waits for us to enter and ask him for compassion. He does not turn us away, so that we need not leave his dwelling, for he has mercy on us.
For it is no ordinary dwelling. It is heaven on earth, because its Lord is within it. In place of the Watchers are pure priests, who invoke the Godhead there.
A dwelling on high, a house below: he is not divided, yet he suffices for all. If you examine him, he is wholly on high; and if you seek him, he is wholly below.
If you are presumptuous, he is high above you; if you love, he is near you. If you investigate, look—he is in heaven; if you believe, look—he is in the sanctuary.
If you seek him as though to seize him, in his height he withdraws beyond your cunning. If you long to see him, in his love he is near your simplicity.
Your strength is weaker than the angels’, yet your rank equals that of the spiritual beings. They have service performed in fear; we have food that is easy for us to receive.
To make himself available to us among earthly beings, he built himself a house among bodily beings. He prepared altars as feeding troughs, at which the Church may eat life.
Let no one [?]. The King is here. Let us enter the sanctuary and see him. Where it is easy for sickness to approach, the physician stands waiting for it.
The fire is hidden and the body is revealed, so that the human hand will not recoil from it. He is awesome in heaven and gentle on earth, so that whoever approaches will not be terrified.
The foundations became holy, and in your living name they laid their stones. Bring righteousness through the gates, whose entrants are gathered in your name.
The courtyards are full of the sound of hosannas, and the dwelling resounds with the sound of hallelujahs. From those outside and those within, praise blazes like torches.
The place is adorned, crowned with glory, for it is a day of festival and feasting. The bridal chamber is new; Christ is the bridegroom. The Watchers rejoice, and human beings give thanks.
The altar is prepared, clothed in truth. The priest stands and molds fire. He takes bread and gives the body; he receives wine and distributes blood.
The altar is made of stones and bears hope. The pure priest calls upon the Spirit. The assembled people cry, “Holy!” The King who hears pours out mercy.
Let the horn of love sound on earth: “Gather your companies to honor the house!” The one who called you gives a reward: new life in the new house.
Whoever labors receives rest, and whoever toils finds life. Whoever makes a vow sees his possessions increase, and whoever fulfills it sees his ventures bear fruit.
Whoever labored with his strength—his body endures. Whoever offered with his hand—his treasure increases. Whoever brought a vowed offering finds hope, and the people who gathered share with them.
For those who labored did so for the sake of those who come, and those who come do so for the sake of those who built. Those who came and those who labored—our Lord made them partners in one reward.
Three gathered in your name are a church; preserve the thousands in your house. For they labored over the church of the heart and brought it to the holy temple built in your name.
May the church within be beautiful, just as the church outside is splendid. Dwell in the one within and preserve the one outside, for heart and house are sealed with [?].
The priests who became a temple of your Spirit worked diligently at building your house. Bless them, for with labor and love they adorned heart and house for your name.
Sustain the priest who built it; prolong his years. May he serve as priest in the dwelling he adorned, and may his soul surpass in hidden beauty the visible adornment that the house bears.
He whose heart carries his Lord’s temple shall enter the house of the holy ones in purity. And when you take pleasure in his intention, grant a reward for laying the foundations.
This visible house proclaims the mind of the one who built it: the heart within is bright and beautiful. His love was revealed in this visible work.
Holy Spirit, listen to the priest who prepared a dwelling for the Father and the Son. Accept the vows along with the offering, for the house and the vows are for your sake.
He prevented David from building, but he encouraged you, and you worked diligently. David, the chosen one, was kept from building the house. Rejoice that you have built it and completed it.
Solomon, who was deemed worthy to build the house, was spared warfare by his Lord. Keep the priests who built a house for Jesus safe from turmoil.
Our Lord gave the whole earth rest from warfare in Solomon’s days. So may our Lord spare the whole church from disputes in your days.
His power could have built a house, just as his command built the created things. He built human beings, and human beings built for him. Glory to his mercies—how greatly they have loved me!
He is without limit, while we are limited. He built a world for us, and we built a house. How great a thing it is that human beings built a house for the power that extends beyond everything!
In his kindness he dwells with us, and as our beloved he draws us toward himself. He lives with us and inspires us all to ascend and live with him.
He departed from his own place and chose a church for himself, so that we might leave our place and choose Eden. God came among human beings so that human beings might be with God.
His altar is prepared, and he reclines with us. He spreads out his glory, and human beings recline. We eat with him at our table; he eats with us at his table.
His honor and greatness are worthy of worship: his body is here, and his reward is there. The altar on earth is filled with his body, while life and glory are in the kingdom.
The disciples took the bread that he blessed and called his body, and the wine his blood. “I have eaten the mystery with you in the church; you will eat with me again in the kingdom.”
Yours, our Lord, is humility: the womb and the manger, the cross and Sheol. Through your love, the riches belong to human beings: heaven and glory, the crown and Eden.

You called our earthly nature to Eden. Your power is in heaven, and your dwelling is on earth. You raised our race so that it might receive glory; you brought your glory down so that it might lift us from disgrace.
The kingdom is yours, and the house is ours, my Lord. Those who built the house received the kingdom. The priest offers bread in your name, and from it you distribute your body to your flock.

Where are you, our Lord? There, in [?]. And where should we seek you? Here, in the sanctuary. Heaven is too high for us, and we cannot reach it. Let us see you in your church, which is accessible to us.
Your throne above is fashioned in fire, and who dares approach it? Your living power dwells in bread, and whoever loves it approaches and tastes.
The faithful see you dwelling in your manger, and your glory woven into swaddling cloths. Eyes fear your rays, yet a hand can easily carry your body.
Oh, how mighty he is, and how kind! Oh, how powerful, and how humble! Oh, how fiercely he burns, and how carefully he protects! Oh, how much he hears, and how much he bears!
In humility he mingles with us, and in kindness he gives his body. Then he sits as judge and passes judgment according to people’s deeds.
He is mighty in heaven and humble on earth. He dwells in the firmament and reclines in a cave. He is clothed in fire and protects his garments. Grumbling [?]. He hears grumbling; his love endures.
The firmament above cannot contain him, yet he dwells in a house, and it bears him. His gaze terrifies Gabriel and his company, yet Mary carried him and remained at peace.
He placed his greatness in his mother’s womb and strengthened her lap to carry the weight. The flame visited the swaddling cloths, and he kept them from burning.
In humility he lay in a manger; in might he threw Babylon into turmoil. The shepherds saw the newborn child; the Magi proclaimed that he was the King of kings.
Let wonder seize Mary too, for every new marvel sprang up and surrounded her. Without union with a man she had a child, and his offerings were pleasing, as befitted a king.
The cave is quiet, and the manger is full. Zion sleeps, and Babylon is awake. She who hated him grew dark at his light; the Church, who loved him, shone at his birth.
A child was born to the daughter of the Levites; the daughters of Jethro took him from her. For she who bore him rejected him, while she who took him recognized him.
He hated his mother because she hated him: although she bore him, she did not love him. He loved the Church, who, when she received him, carried him in her lap and cherished him.
Babylon sent congratulations to Judea. Zion heard and rose up to kill. Through the offerings Babylon sent, envy had beaten a path in Zion.

Travelers were passing along the road; they turned aside and entered her. With their questions they broke her heart. She opened the books, and trembling seized her: the Scriptures numbered her among the ruined.
The scribes who read gave the interpretation: the Messiah would appear in Bethlehem. She who had read them prepared herself, for they brought out for her what she hated.
The star brought the Magi to learn his mystery from the Hebrews. The book she opened taught the Magi the truth about the Son she had borne.
When they reached Judea, they learned that the hardship of their journey was not in vain. They heard the explanation of what had troubled their minds and were confirmed in it.
The star above hid itself. The readers shone out and spoke in its place. It fell silent in heaven when it saw the scribes revealing its mysteries to the people of Babylon.
They opened their books, and its light set. It had come down and shone in their Scriptures. They closed their books, and it showed its rays to the Magi, who had learned who he was.

They traveled along the road, and he was in heaven. They read the books, and he was in the Scriptures. They reached Bethlehem, and he was in the cave. They approached the manger, and he was in swaddling clothes.
His star depicted his divinity and made known that he is hidden and [?]. He shows the way like God and reclines in the manger like a human being.
Heaven carried him onward to Zion. He shone forth in the books in the city of Judea. He is in the Scriptures, and he is in [?], for above and below he is Lord.
The Magi compelled her to rise and learn from her own books what she had forgotten. Micah revealed to her where he would appear; the Magi directed their course there.
As it was read aloud, the Magi learned the route they had come to find. Then they went on confidently, for they had grasped the truth from their books.
She could no longer deny it: her own books had revealed the mystery to her. Her reading became a witness and rebuked the doubt in her mind.
In everything written, glory to your name, Christ, who revealed mysteries to his Church, so that if she goes astray, she may read the prophets and return to the path of faith.
The prophets also spoke about your house, saying that it would be established on the mountaintop. And as we learned concerning it, see, we ourselves have adorned the foundations of your glory.
